                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> be tender.</ns0:note> faint <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>be soft</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>tender.</ns0:hi> Softness or tenderness of heart to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wards God is commended, 2 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 22. 19. but towards ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies it is condemned, here and <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 8. <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 26. 36. 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 13. 7. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 7. 4.</ns0:note>, fear not, and do not <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> make haste.</ns0:note> tremble, neither be ye terrified because of them.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 For the LORD your God <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> he that goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 And the officers shall speak unto the people, saying, What man <ns0:hi>is there</ns0:hi> that hath built a new house, and hath not dedicated it <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Which was done by feasting and thanksgiving to God. See the title of <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 30. and <ns0:hi>Nehem.</ns0:hi> 12. 27. Heb. <ns0:hi>hath initiated it, i. e.</ns0:hi> entred upon it, taken possession of it, dwelt in it.</ns0:note>? let him go and return to his house <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Least his heart be set upon it, and thereby he be negligent or timerous in the battel to the scandal and prejudice of others.</ns0:note>, lest he die in the battel, and another man dedicate it <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">And so he should lose and another get the fruit of his labours, which might seem unjust or hard. And God provides even for mens infirmities. But this and the following exceptions are to be understood onely of a War al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowed by God, not in a War commanded by God, not in the approaching war with the <ns0:hi>Canaanites,</ns0:hi> from which even the Bridegroom was not exempted, as the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> writers note.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 And what man <ns0:hi>is he</ns0:hi> that hath planted a vine<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />yard <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">This and the former dispensation were generally convenient<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but more necessary in the beginning of their settlement in <ns0:hi>Ca<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />naan,</ns0:hi> for the encouragement of those who should build houses or plant vineyards, which was chargeable to them, and benefi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cial to the commonwealth.</ns0:note>, and hath not yet <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>made it common.</ns0:hi> See Lev. 19. 23, 24.</ns0:note> eaten of it <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>made it common,</ns0:hi> to wit, for the use of himself and family and friends, which it was not till the fifth year, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 19. 23, &c. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 31. 5.</ns0:note>? let him <ns0:hi>also</ns0:hi> go and return unto his house, lest he die in the battel, and another man eat of it.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 24. 5.</ns0:note> And what man <ns0:hi>is there</ns0:hi> that hath betroth<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Which was done by a solemn and mutual promise, but not by an actual contract. See <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 19. 14. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 22. 23.</ns0:note> a wife, and hath not taken her? let him go and return unto his house, lest he die in the bat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tel, and another man take her.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And the officers shall speak further unto the people: and they shall say, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Judg. 7. 3.</ns0:note> What man <ns0:hi>is there that is</ns0:hi> fearfull and faint-hearted? let him go and return unto his house, lest his brethrens heart <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> melt.</ns0:note> faint as well as his heart.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 And it shall be when the officers have made an end of speaking unto the people, that they shall make captains of the armies <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. to be <ns0:hi>i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap> the head of the people.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> to lead the people <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Or rather, as the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> hath it, <ns0:hi>they shall set</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>place the captains of the armies in the head or front of the people</ns0:hi> under their charge, that they may conduct and manage them, and by their example incourage their souldiers. But it is not likely they had their captains to make or chuse when they were just going to battel.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 When thou comest nigh unto a city to fight against it, then <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Sam. 20. 18.</ns0:note> proclaim peace unto it <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">This seems to be understood not of the cities of the <ns0:hi>Ca<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />naanites,</ns0:hi> as is manifest from <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 16, 17, 18. who were under an absolute sentence of utter destruction, <ns0:hi>Exod</ns0:hi> 23. 32, 33. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 7. 1, 2. whence they are blamed that made any league or peace with them, <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 2. 2. but of the cities either of other nations who injured or disturbed them, or commen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ced war against them, or aided their enemies, or oppressed their friends and allies; or of the <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi> themselves, if they were guilty or abettors of Idolatry or Apostacy from God, or of sedition or rebellion against authority, or of giving protecti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on and defence to capital offenders. See <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 14. <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 20. 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 20. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 And it shall be, if it make thee answer of peace, and open unto thee, then it shall be, <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> all the people <ns0:hi>that is</ns0:hi> found therein, shall be tribu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />taries unto thee, and they shall serve thee <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">By their purses, and by their labours too, as appears from 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 9. 15. 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 8. 7.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 And if it will make no peace with thee<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but will make war against thee, then thou shalt be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />siege it.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 And <ns0:hi>when</ns0:hi> the LORD thy God hath deli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vered it into thine hand, thou shalt smite every male thereof with the edg of the sword <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">A just punishment of their obstinate refusal of peace offered.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 But the women, and the little ones <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Excused by their sex or age, as not involved in the guilt, nor being likely to revenge their quarrel.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Josh. 8. 2.</ns0:note> the cattel, and all that is in the city, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> all the spoil thereof, shalt thou <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> spoil.</ns0:note> take unto thy self, and thou shalt eat the spoil of thine enemies, which the LORD thy God hath given thee.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 Thus shalt thou do unto all the cities <ns0:hi>which are</ns0:hi> very far off from thee, which <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> not of the cities of these nations.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Num. 33. 5<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>. chap. 7. 1, 2.</ns0:note> of the cities of these people which the LORD thy God doth give thee <ns0:hi>for</ns0:hi> an inheri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tance, thou shalt save alive nothing that breath<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>no soul, i. e.</ns0:hi> no man, as that word is oft used. Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pare <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 10. 40. with 11. 14. For the beasts, some few ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cepted as being under a special curse, were given them for a prey.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:159" />17 But thou shalt utterly destroy them, <ns0:hi>namely,</ns0:hi> the Hittites, and the Amorites, the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, as the LORD thy God hath commanded thee:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 That they teach you not to do after all their abominations which they have done unto their gods: so should ye sin against the LORD your God.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 When thou shalt besiege a city a long time in making war against it, to take it, thou shalt not destroy the trees thereof <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">To wit, the fruit trees, as appears from the following words. Which is to be understood of a general destruction of them, not of the cutting down of some few of them, as the conveni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ency of the siege might require.</ns0:note>, by forcing an ax against them, for thou mayest eat of them, and thou shalt not cut them down (<ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>for, O man, the tree of the field</ns0:hi> is <ns0:hi>to be im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ployed in the siege.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> for the tree of the field is mans <ns0:hi>life</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>(i. e.)</ns0:hi> The sustenance or support of his life, as <ns0:hi>life</ns0:hi> is taken <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 24. 6. But this place may be otherwise translated, as it is in the Margent of our <ns0:hi>Eng<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lish</ns0:hi> Bibles: <ns0:hi>For, O man</ns0:hi> (the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> letter <ns0:hi>He</ns0:hi> being here the note of a vocative case, as it is <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 9. 7.) <ns0:hi>the tree</ns0:hi> (or, <ns0:hi>trees,</ns0:hi> the singular number for the plural, as is common) <ns0:hi>of the field</ns0:hi> is (or ought, as the <ns0:hi>Hebrew Lamed</ns0:hi> is used <ns0:hi>Esth.</ns0:hi> 9. 1. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 62. 10.) <ns0:hi>to be employed in the siege,</ns0:hi> or, as it is in the <ns0:hi>Hebrew, to go be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore thy face, i. e.</ns0:hi> to make fences for thy security, <ns0:hi>in the siege. The trees of the field,</ns0:hi> I here understand not in its general signifi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cation of all trees including fruit-bearing trees, as that phrase is commonly used, but in its more special and distinct significati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on, for unfruitful trees as it is taken <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 55. 1 2. or such as grow one<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly in open fields, such as are elsewhere called <ns0:hi>the trees of the wood,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 16. 33. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 7. 2. or <ns0:hi>the trees of the forest, Cant.</ns0:hi> 2. 3. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 10. 19. which are opposed to the trees of the gardens, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 3. 2, 8. <ns0:hi>Eccl.</ns0:hi> 2. 5. <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 31. 9. as the <ns0:hi>flower of the field, Psal.</ns0:hi> 103. 15. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 40. 6. and <ns0:hi>the lilies of the field, Mat.</ns0:hi> 6. 28. are opposed to those that grow in Gardens, and are preserved and cultivated by the gardeners art and care. And so it is a very proper argu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment to disswade from the destroying of fruit-trees, because the wild and unfruitful trees were sufficient for the use of the siege. And this sence fitly agrees with the following words, where the concession or grant which here is delivered in more ambiguous terms of <ns0:hi>the tree of the field</ns0:hi> is repeated and explained concern<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing <ns0:hi>the trees which thou knowest that they</ns0:hi> be <ns0:hi>not trees for meat.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> to go from before thee.</ns0:note> to imploy them in the siege.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 Onely the trees which thou knowest that they <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> not trees for meat, thou shalt destroy, and cut them down, and thou shalt build bulwarks a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst the city that maketh war with thee, until <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> it come down.</ns0:note> it be subdued.</ns0:p>
